rule: These entries are concurrent prompts. No entry overrides exact arithmetic or proves its own construction history.

0.gloss: Zero may be a numeric identity, empty state, inactive state, or port; inspect the carrier type.

1.gloss: One may be acting as the seed of the double-plus-one ancestry 1 -> 3 -> 7 -> 15.

2.gloss: Two may be acting as a gap or span receipt between named endpoints.

3.gloss: Three may announce a nine shadow; the exact decimal receipt is 3 squared equals 9.
3.missing: adapter if used beyond decimal squaring

4.gloss: Four may be a square, a midpoint, or a four-slot lock depending on the receiver.

5.gloss: Five may be acting as the half-base endpoint or as the held-still N coordinate.

6.gloss: Six may be wearing a computed-corner role instead of arriving as an independent source coordinate.

7.gloss: Seven may be an all-on three-bit address or the last pre-seam node of 1 -> 3 -> 7.

8.gloss: Eight may be inspected as two four-coordinates with one candidate shadow or negative-half role.
8.missing: named fold, sign, or abduction receiver; coordinate duplication alone is insufficient

9.gloss: Nine may be a decimal minus-one residue or the column immediately before a successor carry.

sequences.gloss: Nine beside one can prompt the carry-brink lens; the exact receipt is 9 + 1 = 10, not adjacency by itself.
Three beside nine can prompt a root-square lens because 3 squared equals 9.
This digit set differs from its P-image only by toggling membership across the orbit {2,8}.
sequences.missing: receiver showing why that single-orbit vacancy predicts anything downstream
